The answer correctly makes s.4(1) decisive and states the s.83/s.82 fines accurately, but it never applies s.4(1) to the facts: the exemption turns on the collector's purpose (personal benefit or household activity only), which a home security camera ordinarily meets, yet the headline says it may be illegal and fined in the millions and treats the camera's view of a public road as possibly defeating the exemption, a limit the statute does not contain.

problems.why: Section 4(1) exempts collection, use or disclosure by a person who collects for personal benefit or household activity only; the test is the purpose, and the text says nothing about where the data is captured or whether other people in a public place appear.

conclusion_reason: Every rule cited is accurate and s.4(1) is applied, but the answer declines to conclude; a camera at one's own home for one's own security is collection for personal benefit, so under s.4(1) the Act does not apply and no million-baht fine arises, which the answer leaves open while stressing the fines.

Under s.4(1) the Act does not apply to collection for purely personal or household purposes, so incidental capture of others is not a PDPA violation in that case; outside it, ss.19/24/27 and the penalties in ss.79/83/84 apply as stated.
